pencereler.0-5: In a violent storm, the world's largest semi-submersible rig capsized. The crew abandoned it,
pencereler.5-12: and all eighty four men died. It started with one broken porthole. Seawater flooded the ballast control panel. The
pencereler.12-20: panel shorted, and valves began acting on their own. The rig tilted forward, and water entered its chain lockers. It rolled over
pencereler.20-30: before dawn. Rig ballast systems, training and survival gear were improved.

segmentler.metin: The Ocean Ranger capsized in a storm off Newfoundland.
It took only a wave breaking a porthole in the ballast control room.
So how could a wave breaking a porthole in the ballast control room do this?

The answer is seawater shorting the ballast control panel, followed by wrong ballast valve operation and flooding — and it is why offshore rigs got better ballast system design, training and survival gear.
